market_summary: US September CPI came in hot: headline +0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y (3.6% expected, 3.4% in August), core +0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y (0.2% and 2.5% expected), with gasoline +9.1% m/m doing over half the work; CME FedWatch odds of an Oct 28 hike rose to about 32-37% from 22% (briefly near 49%). Wednesday's US close: S&P 500 -1.11% to 7,718.94, Nasdaq -1.88% to 26,692.87 (worst day since July 23), Dow -0.09% to 51,621.48; the chip index fell 4.3% for a sixth straight loss and AI-debt names were hit hardest (CoreWeave -15%, Nebius -10%, Oracle -8.8%, Dell -11.4%, Nvidia about -3%, Micron about -4%); Bank of America fell 4.8% after a $1.2B money-laundering fine cut EPS to $0.91, and Morgan Stanley about -3% despite EPS of $3.03 (from $2.80). Thursday in Asia the chip rout spread: KOSPI -7.57% to 5,554.22 after a 20-minute circuit breaker (SK hynix and Samsung down about 10-11%), Nikkei -4.90% to 64,425.95 (SoftBank -9%, Kioxia -11%), Taiex -3.41% to 46,969.87, Shanghai about -1.6% and Shenzhen about -1.9% to their lowest since August 2025, Hang Seng about -1.3% in the afternoon and the ASX 200 only -0.1% at 8,715.6; an IMF report warned an AI correction would hit Asia hardest. Australia lost 39,300 jobs in September against a 19,600 gain expected, unemployment held at 4.7% (4.6% expected) and participation fell to 66.8%, trimming the case for a November RBA hike. TSMC reported a sixth straight record quarter after the Taipei close, net profit NT$763.06B (+68.7% y/y, above estimates); its shares had fallen 2.2% before the release. At 17:52 AEDT S&P 500 futures were -0.4%, Nasdaq 100 -1.1% and Dow +0.1%; Brent was about $104.7 and WTI $94.1 (both about -1.3%) after settling near $106.06 and $95.09 Wednesday on a Houthi strike on an Aramco office building; gold futures about $4,160 (+1.3%); bitcoin about $80,850 (-3.2% in 24h). Next: US PPI, retail sales, jobless claims, Philly Fed and Empire State 23:30 AEDT tonight; US open 00:30 AEDT Fri; Fed's Hammack 07:30 AEDT Fri; Warsh with the IMF's Georgieva 14:30 AEDT Fri; options expiry Fri US (07:00 AEDT Sat close); FOMC blackout from Sat Oct 17; China Q3 GDP 13:00 AEDT Mon Oct 19; Netflix 07:01 AEDT Wed Oct 21; Meta and TI 07:30, IBM and Lam 08:00, Tesla 08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22; AU CPI 11:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28; Fed decision 05:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29; Alphabet 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 29 and Microsoft the same evening US; US Q3 GDP and September PCE 23:30 AEDT Thu Oct 29.

AMZN.reason: Down 1.7% Wednesday, a fourth straight decline, in line with the hot-CPI tech selloff (Nasdaq -1.9%). No follow-up found on the WSJ-reported Decart talks (about $7 billion, unsigned). PPI, retail sales and claims tonight 23:30 AEDT; Q3 about Fri Oct 30 07:00 AEDT. Hold.

AXOS.reason: Down 2.0% Wednesday as hot CPI (3.7% y/y, core 2.6%) lifted Fed hike odds and banks sold off: Bank of America fell 4.8% on a revenue miss and a $1.2 billion-plus fine. Futures put about 37% odds on an Oct 28 hike. PPI and retail sales tonight 23:30 AEDT; Axos fiscal Q1 Fri Oct 30 08:00 AEDT. Hold.

BABA.reason: US ADR up 0.3% Wednesday, one of few gainers. Hong Kong turned lower Thursday on US rate-hike bets: Alibaba was down nearly 2% at the open and the Hang Seng closed down 1.4%. No company news; China Q3 GDP Mon Oct 19 13:00 AEDT. Hold.

ENPH.reason: Fell 8.4% Wednesday, wiping out Tuesday's 1.7% gain, as the hot CPI hit rate-sensitive names. The 10-year yield spiked above 5.32% before easing to about 5.19%. Q3 call Wed Oct 28 07:30 AEDT. Watch.

FIGR.reason: Fell 8.1% Wednesday after 4.3% Tuesday, about 12% in two sessions, and is back near its 52-week low with no company news found. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year actually eased to 7.45%, so this was risk-off selling, not a rate move. PPI tonight 23:30 AEDT; Q3 date still unannounced. Hold, but this is close to a watch.

GOOGL.reason: Down 1.7% Wednesday, slightly better than the Nasdaq's 1.9%. No company news. TSMC's Q3 beat and Q4 guide of $52.3-54.3 billion (about 14% higher at the midpoint) show AI chip demand still rising, which supports the Google Cloud and TPU build-out. Q3 results Oct 28. Add stays.

LDI.reason: Fell 10.7% Wednesday, a second straight heavy loss (about 15% over two sessions), even though Mortgage News Daily's 30-year eased 0.01 points to 7.45%. Hot CPI (core 2.6%) pushed Fed hike odds to about 91% by December, which keeps mortgage rates near three-year highs. Still below the NYSE one-dollar threshold. Trim.

META.reason: Fell 3.3% Wednesday, giving back Tuesday's 2.6% Muse Wonder gain as communication services fell 1.7%. No New Mexico privacy penalty ruling found yet. Q3 results Wed Oct 21 after the US close, call 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Fell 8.7% Wednesday with no company news found, as the chip index dropped 4.3% for a sixth straight day and AI-infrastructure names sold off (CoreWeave -15%, Oracle -8.8%). TSMC's Thursday results support custom-chip demand: HPC rose to 68% of revenue and Q4 is guided about 14% higher. Hold.

MU.reason: Moved from hold: fell 4.1% Wednesday, a fourth straight loss and about 11% since Oct 9, and the memory rout deepened in Asia Thursday as KOSPI closed down 7.6% after a circuit breaker, with SK hynix -11% and Samsung about -10%. TSMC's strong AI outlook has not lifted memory names, though DDR5 spot set another high. Taiwan union rally Mon Oct 19, mediation Thu Oct 22. Watch.

NFLX.reason: Up 0.2% Wednesday on a down day. Co-CEOs Sarandos and Peters confirmed about 6% job cuts (nearly 1,000 roles, mostly product, tech, legal and HR), the largest since 2022, and said the company is on track for its full-year forecast. Q3 results Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT. Hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: Fell 3.2% Wednesday on hot CPI, IDC data showing its China AI-chip share fell to 34% in the first half, and Microsoft's Maia 300 in-house chip plan for 2027. TSMC's Thursday beat (HPC 68% of revenue, Q4 guided about 14% higher) supports demand. GTC Berlin Oct 20-22. Hold.

RKT.reason: Down 2.8% Wednesday, a fifth straight decline and another 52-week low, even as Mortgage News Daily's 30-year eased to 7.45%. Hot CPI raised December hike odds to about 91%, which keeps refinancing demand weak. PPI and retail sales tonight 23:30 AEDT; Q3 around Oct 29. Watch.

TSM.reason: TSMC beat Thursday: Q3 revenue $46.72 billion (+41% y/y) above its $44.6-45.8 billion guide, gross margin 66.4% within 65-67%, EPS up 69%, and Q4 guided to $52.3-54.3 billion at 65-67% margin. The ADR fell 3.4% Wednesday and Taipei shares 2.0% Thursday, both before the release; the ADR reacts from 00:30 AEDT Fri. Add stays.

STRIPE.reason: No new round, tender or secondary mark found; the last company tender was February at $159 billion, so the mark multiple stays 2.27. No company news found for Oct 14-15. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: No close reported for the roughly $30 billion round at about $1.4 trillion pre-money, so the mark multiple stays 5.43. At Anthropic's Oct 14 investor session it reportedly showed Q3 revenue of $16.8 billion (+45% q/q) and an adjusted profit, a high bar for OpenAI's round. Hold.

headlines: Hot US CPI (3.7%, core 2.6%) sank the Nasdaq 1.9% and chips 4.3%; Marvell -8.7%, loanDepot -10.7%, Enphase -8.4%.
Asia chip rout Thursday: KOSPI -7.6% after a circuit breaker, SK hynix -11%, Nikkei -4.9%; Micron moved from hold to watch.
TSMC beat after Taipei closed: Q4 guided to $52.3-54.3B against $48.8B expected; the ADR reacts from 00:30 AEDT Fri.
CoreWeave fell 15% as its 2032 bonds dropped below 78c; the neocloud-credit bellwether flips to bearish.
Anthropic reportedly told investors Q3 revenue was $16.8B and adjusted-profitable; IPO marketing could start the week of Nov 9.
Next: US PPI and retail sales 23:30 AEDT tonight; China Q3 GDP Mon 13:00 AEDT; Netflix results Wed 07:00 AEDT.
